items.title: 66960_Gil Evans oral history interview
items.q: Miles and I were writing a score for a play at the time that Lawrence Harvey was going to play in.

ctx.x:
a ticket.
Well that ended up with him wanting to search everybody and he's been saying to me, what do you do? And I said, well I'm a composer. And he said, well I hope you don't write jazz, something like that. Imagine a cop bothering to say that to me.

He's got Harold up against the car and Harold's turned around. It's really fantastic over nothing.
It was because we were all mixed together that was it. We were all mixed together. There were a couple of, Miles and I were writing a score for a play at the time that Lawrence Harvey was going to play in. Lawrence Harvey was there, (he was an actor, a famous actor?). It was a mixture like that and that policeman took it upon himself to be the cultural dictator besides the social director of the city. (LAUGHTER).
They really do that, they really do that.
